A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SurFhead study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FaceTalk and NeRSemble evaluations, component ablations, and qualitative reconstruction and relighting results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds a Gaussian Head Avatars comparison, additional ablation controls and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 changes the auxiliary vertex's normal offset: the edge cross product is divided by its Euclidean norm in v1 and by its square-root magnitude in v2. This revises the stated edge-matrix/Jacobian construction. The surfel representation, JBS blending, eyeball components and losses otherwise remain.

E1.justification: Both versions retain FaceTalk and NeRSemble, the same reconstruction, reenactment and novel-view tasks, and the existing extreme-expression, relighting and mesh demonstrations. The added comparisons do not establish new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Gaussian Head Avatars (GHA; Xu et al., 2024), previously cited without an evaluated comparison, is added in v2 Table 6 and Figure 8. GaussianAvatars also becomes an explicit comparator in Table 3's ablation experiment and the new timing comparison. Existing benchmark comparators remain.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds an unaugmented 2DGS-plus-GaussianAvatars control; v1's eye-equipped Vanilla configuration is retained as '+ eyeballs'. The new timing evaluation measures FPS and training hours across components and compares PyTorch SVD with RoMA Procrustes. Existing dataset splits, quality metrics and the 300,000-iteration training schedule remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The expanded Table 3 isolates eye modeling relative to the newly reported unaugmented baseline. Appendix A.5 adds component-level computational-cost analysis and experimentally tests the RoMA alternative that v1 only suggested. Existing Jacobian, JBS, eye and teeth ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experiments. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and matched Table 3 configurations retain their values; Table 3 adds GaussianAvatars and the bare Vanilla control. New Table 6 reports GHA/SurFhead PSNR of 27.25/26.20 and NCS of 0.505/0.837. Table 7 adds timings, including SurFhead at 90.13 FPS, 94.72 FPS with RoMA, and 2.11 training hours. These are additional results, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: The auxiliary-vertex definition in Section 2.2 changes its normalization, altering the formal edge matrix underlying the Jacobian. The inverse-transpose normal derivation and Appendix A.2 proofs of polar-decomposition uniqueness and covariance positive semidefiniteness are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same central claims about geometrically accurate Gaussian head avatars, affine/JBS deformation, eye modeling and extreme-pose performance. The additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix A.4 adds explanations attributing GHA artifacts to screen-space refinement, while A.5 interprets measured runtime overhead as arising mainly from polar decomposition. Existing FLAME-expression and hair limitations remain. The new ethics statement also states an academic-research-only intended-use restriction.

D1.justification: v2 adds project and code links and a reproducibility statement identifying GaussianAvatars' preprocessed NeRSemble data. It also documents training times, the cuSOLVER-backed PyTorch SVD implementation and the tested RoMA replacement. Existing optimization hyperparameters and ASG implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a neural-surface-reconstruction discussion covering work such as NeuS, Neuralangelo, H3D-Net and MonoNPHM, explicitly positioning SurFhead's Gaussian approach against SDF-based reconstruction. This extends the background without replacing its original research positioning. SMPL and RoMA bibliographic updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the JBS explanation, clarifies the adjacency notation, and adds acknowledgment, reproducibility and ethics statements plus an additional-experiment subsection. Most prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7 and the GHA comparison in Figure 8, expands Table 3, revises Figure 2b and its caption, and adds conference headers. Existing appendix illustrations are retained with relocation and renumbering; the overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: The additional ablation controls, GHA comparison and component timings strengthen the evidence beyond v1, particularly by turning its speculative efficiency discussion into measured analysis. Code-access information and expanded research context also improve usability. These are limited gains: the new comparison and timing conditions remain incompletely specified, and the PDFs do not explain whether the revised geometry formula affected the reported experiments.
